source_text: Ἂν ἐνταῦθα διατρίβῃς συνεχῶς, καὶ ἅπερ ἔλαβες ἔξωθεν κακὰ ἀποθήσῃ πάντως· ἂν δὲ ἀποπηδᾷς καὶ φεύγῃς καὶ ἅπερ ἐκτήσω παρὰ τῶν θείων Γραφῶν ἀγαθὰ ἀπολεῖς πάντως, κατὰ μικρὸν ἐκ τῶν ἔξω συνεδρίων καὶ διαλέξεων ὑποσυρομένης σου τῆς εὐπορίας. Καὶ ὅτι ταῦτά ἐστιν ἀληθῆ, ἀνα χωροῦντες ἐντεῦθεν σπουδάσατε τοὺς σήμερον ἀπολειφθέντας ἰδεῖν, καὶ ὄψεσθε πόσον τὸ μέσον τῆς ὑμετέρας εὐθυμίας καὶ τῆς ἐκείνων ἀθυμίας. Οὐχ οὕτως ἐστὶ νύμφη καλὴ καὶ ἐπίχαρις ἐν παστάδι καθημένη, ὡς ἔστι ψυχὴ θαυμαστὴ καὶ ἔνδοξος ἐν Ἐκκλησίᾳ φαινομένη, μύρων πνέουσα πνευματικῶν. Ὁ γὰρ ἐνταῦθα μετὰ πίστεως καὶ σπουδῆς παραγινόμενος, μυρίους λαβὼν ἄπεισι θησαυρούς· κἂν ἀνοίξῃ τὸ στόμα μόνον, πάσης εὐωδίας εὐθέως καὶ πλούτου πνευματικοῦ τοὺς συγγινομένους ἐνέπλησε κἂν μυρία προσπέσῃ δεινὰ, πάντα οἴσει ῥᾳδίως, ἱκανὴν ἀφορμὴν ἀπὸ τῶν θείων Γραφῶν ὑπομονῆς καὶ φιλοσοφίας ἐντεῦθεν λαβών. Καὶ καθάπερ ὁ διηνεκῶς ἐπὶ τῆς πέτρας ἑστὼς τῶν κυμάτων καταγελᾷ, οὕτως ὁ συνάξεως ἀπολαύων διηνεκοῦς, καὶ τοῖς θείοις ἀρδευόμενος λόγοις, καθάπερ ἐπὶ πέτρας τῆς ὀρθῆς τῶν πραγμάτων κρίσεως στήσας ἑαυ τὸν, οὐδενὶ τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων ἁλώσεται, ἀνώτερον τῆς τῶν βιωτικῶν πραγμάτων καταστήσας ἑαυτὸν ἐπιδρομῆς· οὐκ ἀπὸ συμβουλῆς δὲ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀπὸ εὐχῆς, καὶ ἀπὸ πατρικῆς εὐλογίας, καὶ ἀπὸ κοινῆς συνόδου, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἀγάπης, καὶ ἐξ ἑτέρων μυρίων πολλὴν ὠφέλειαν καὶ ψυχαγωγίαν καρπωσάμενος, οὕτως ἀνεχώρησε, μυρία οἴκαδε φέρων ἀγαθά. Ὅρα οὖν πόσης μὲν ὑμεῖς σήμερον ἀπολαύσεσθε τῆς εὐλογίας, πόσην δὲ ὑποστήσονται ἐκεῖνοι τὴν ζημίαν. Ὑμεῖς μὲν γὰρ μαρτύρων μισθὸν λαμβάνοντες ἀπελεύσεσθε· ἐκεῖνοι δὲ πρὸς τῷ τοῦ κέρδους ἀποστερηθῆναι τούτου, καὶ ἑτέραν ὑποστήσονται ζημίαν, ἐκ τῶν ἀνονήτων διατριβῶν πολὺν φροντίδων ἐπισυρόμενοι φορυτόν. Ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ δεχό μενος προφήτην εἰς ὄνομα προφήτου, μισθὸν προφήτου λήψεται, καὶ ὁ δεχόμενος δίκαιον εἰς ὄνομα δικαίου, μισθὸν δικαίου λήψεται· οὕτως ὁ δεχόμενος μάρτυρα εἰς ὄνομα μάρτυρος, μισθὸν μάρτυρος λήψεται· ὑποδοχὴ δὲ μάρτυρος τὸ συνελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ἐκείνου μνήμην, τὸ κοινωνῆσαι τῆς διηγήσεως τῶν ἄθλων, τὸ θαυμάσαι τὰ γεγενημένα, τὸ ζηλῶσαι τὴν ἀρετὴν, τὸ εἰς ἑτέρους ἐξενεγκεῖν τὰς ἀνδραγαθίας τὰς ἐκείνου· ταῦτα τῶν μαρτύρων τὰ ξένια· οὕτω τοὺς ἁγίους τούτους τις ὑποδέχεται, καθάπερ οὖν καὶ ὑμεῖς τήμερον πεποιήκατε. βʹ. Χθὲς μὲν οὖν ὁ Δεσπότης ἡμῶν ὕδατι ἐβαπτίσατο, σήμερον δὲ ὁ δοῦλος αἵματι βαπτίζεται· χθὲς ἠνεῴχθησαν οὐρανοῦ πύλαι, σήμερον κατεπατήθησαν ᾅδου πύ λαι. Καὶ μὴ θαυμάσητε, εἰ βάπτισμα τὸ μαρτύριον ἐκάλεσα· καὶ γὰρ καὶ ἐνταῦθα τὸ Πνεῦμα μετὰ πολ λῆς ἐφίπταται τῆς δαψιλείας, καὶ ἁμαρτημάτων ἀναίρεσις καὶ ψυχῆς γίνεται καθαρμὸς θαυμαστός τις καὶ παράδοξος· καὶ ὥσπερ οἱ βαπτιζόμενοι τοῖς ὕδα σιν, οὕτως οἱ μαρτυροῦντες τῷ ἰδίῳ λούονται αἵματι· ὃ δὴ καὶ ἐπὶ τούτου γεγένηται. Ἀλλὰ γὰρ πρὸ τῆς σφαγῆς ἀναγκαῖον εἰπεῖν τοῦ διαβόλου τὴν πανουρ γίαν. Συνιδὼν γὰρ ἐκεῖνος ὅτι πάσης τιμωρίας καὶ κολάσεως εἴδους κατεγέλασε, καὶ οὔτε κάμινον ἀν άψας, οὔτε βάραθρον ὀρύξας, οὔτε τροχὸν εὐτρεπίσας, οὔτε εἰς ξύλον ἀναγαγὼν, οὔτε εἰς κρημνοὺς ῥίψας, οὔτε εἰς θηρίων ὀδόντας ἐμβαλὼν ἴσχυσε περιγενέσθαι τῆς τοῦ ἁγίου φιλοσοφίας, ἕτερον ἐπενόησε χαλεπώ τερον τρόπον, καὶ περιῄει ζητῶν τιμωρίαν εὑρεῖν, ὥστε τὴν αὐτὴν ὁμοῦ καὶ δριμυτάτην γενέσθαι καὶ μακροτάτην.
thought_title: The church's profit and the martyr's baptism
orientation: Chrysostom is still addressing the congregation that stayed for the feast, contrasting their gain with the loss of those who left, and now begins to turn to the martyr Lucian.
pass_a_gloss: If you spend time here continually, then also the evils which you received from outside you will put away entirely; but if you leap away and flee, then also the goods which you acquired from the divine Scriptures you will lose entirely, your wealth being gradually dragged away by the assemblies and conversations outside. And that these things are true, when you go up from here, make haste to see those who were left behind today, and you will see how great is the distance between your cheerfulness and their despondency. A bride fair and charming sitting in her bridal chamber is not so beautiful as a soul wondrous and glorious appearing in the Church, breathing spiritual perfumes. For the one who comes here with faith and zeal, having received ten thousand treasures, departs; and if he opens only his mouth, immediately he fills those who are with him with all fragrance and spiritual wealth; and if ten thousand terrible things befall him, he will bear all things easily, having received from here from the divine Scriptures a sufficient starting-point of endurance and self-discipline. And just as the one who stands continually on the rock laughs at the waves, so the one who enjoys continual assembly, and is watered by the divine words, having set himself as on a rock of right judgment of things, will be taken by none of human things, having set himself above the assault of worldly affairs; and not from counsel only, but also from prayer, and from a fatherly blessing, and from the common gathering, and from the love of the brothers, and from ten thousand other things, having reaped much benefit and refreshment of soul, so he departed, carrying home ten thousand good things. See therefore how much blessing you will enjoy today, and how much loss those others will undergo. For you will depart receiving a martyr's reward; but they, in addition to being deprived of this gain, will also undergo another loss, dragging along with them from their useless pastimes a great heap of cares. For just as the one who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward, and the one who receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man's reward; so the one who receives a martyr in the name of a martyr will receive a martyr's reward; and the receiving of a martyr is to come together for his remembrance, to share in the narration of his contests, to marvel at what happened, to emulate his virtue, to carry out to others his brave deeds; these are the gifts of hospitality for the martyrs; thus one receives these holy ones, just as indeed you also have done today. 2. Yesterday then our Master was baptized with water, but today the servant is baptized with blood; yesterday the gates of heaven were opened, today the gates of Hades were trampled down. And do not be amazed if I called the martyrdom a baptism; for indeed here also the Spirit hovers over with much abundance, and a removal of sins and a cleansing of the soul happens, wondrous and extraordinary; and just as those who are baptized with waters, so those who bear witness are washed with their own blood; which indeed has also happened in the case of this man. But before the slaughter it is necessary to speak of the devil's cunning. For that one, seeing that he laughed at every form of punishment and chastisement, and neither by kindling a furnace, nor by digging a pit, nor by preparing a wheel, nor by leading him up onto wood, nor by casting him down cliffs, nor by throwing him into the teeth of wild beasts was he able to overcome the self-discipline of the holy man, devised another harsher method, and went about seeking to find a punishment, so that the same punishment might be at once both most piercing and most prolonged.

choices.why: The glossary requires self-discipline for φιλοσοφία, here referring to the holy man's disciplined endurance.
The glossary requires martyrdom for μαρτύριον, understood as a baptism in blood.
The phrase echoes the dominical saying about receiving a prophet or righteous man; rendering μισθός as reward keeps the parallel structure clear.
ξένια are gifts given to a guest; rendering as gifts of hospitality preserves the metaphor of receiving the martyr as a guest.
The glossary requires contest for ἄθλησις; here the plural ἄθλων refers to the martyr's struggles, so contests keeps the athletic image.
ἀνδραγαθία means manly excellence or brave deeds; rendering as brave deeds fits the context of carrying out the martyr's exploits to others.

pass_b_english: If you spend time here continually, you will certainly put away whatever evils you picked up outside; but if you jump away and flee, you will certainly lose whatever good things you acquired from the divine Scriptures, as your wealth is gradually dragged away by the gatherings and conversations outside. And that these things are true—when you leave here, make a point of seeing those who stayed away today, and you will see how great the distance is between your cheerfulness and their despondency. A beautiful and charming bride sitting in her bridal chamber is not so lovely as a wondrous and glorious soul appearing in the Church, breathing spiritual perfumes. For the one who comes here with faith and zeal departs carrying away ten thousand treasures; and if he only opens his mouth, he immediately fills those who are with him with every fragrance and spiritual wealth. And if ten thousand terrible things fall upon him, he will bear them all easily, having received from here from the divine Scriptures ample resources for endurance and self-discipline. And just as the one who stands continually on the rock laughs at the waves, so the one who enjoys continual assembly and is watered by the divine words, having set himself as on a rock of right judgment about things, will not be captured by any human thing, having placed himself above the assault of worldly affairs. And not from counsel only, but also from prayer, and from a father's blessing, and from the common gathering, and from the love of the brothers and sisters, and from ten thousand other things, he reaps much benefit and refreshment of soul, and so departs, carrying home ten thousand good things. See, then, how much blessing you will enjoy today, and how much loss they will endure. For you will go away receiving a martyr's reward; but they, besides being deprived of this gain, will also endure another loss, dragging along with themselves from their useless pastimes a great heap of cares. For just as the one who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward, and the one who receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person's reward (Matthew 10:41), so the one who receives a martyr in the name of a martyr will receive a martyr's reward. And receiving a martyr means gathering for his remembrance, sharing in the telling of his contests, marveling at what happened, imitating his virtue, and carrying his brave deeds out to others. These are the gifts of hospitality for the martyrs; this is how one receives these holy ones—just as you have done today.

Yesterday our Master was baptized in water; today the servant is baptized in blood. Yesterday the gates of heaven were opened; today the gates of hell were trampled down. And do not be surprised that I called martyrdom a baptism; for here too the Spirit hovers over with great abundance, and there is a removal of sins and a wondrous and extraordinary cleansing of the soul. And just as those who are baptized are washed in water, so those who bear witness are washed in their own blood—which is exactly what happened in this case. But before the slaughter, it is necessary to speak of the devil's cunning. For when he saw that the holy man laughed at every kind of punishment and torture, and that neither by lighting a furnace, nor digging a pit, nor preparing a wheel, nor leading him up to a wooden stake, nor hurling him down cliffs, nor casting him into the teeth of wild beasts was he able to overcome the holy man's self-discipline, he devised another, harsher method, and went around seeking to find a punishment that would be at once both the sharpest and the longest.

last_rejected.ruling: English 'when you leave here' renders ἀναχωροῦντες ἐντεῦθεν accurately as temporal participle; not a command in Greek.

last_rejected.quote: dragging along with themselves from their useless pastimes a great heap of cares
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐκ τῶν ἀνονήτων διατριβῶν πολὺν φροντίδων ἐπισυρόμενοι φορυτόν
last_rejected.why: ἀνονήτων διατριβῶν means 'useless occupations/activities,' not 'pastimes' (too light); φορυτόν is 'dust/chaff,' not 'heap'—the image is of choking dust, not a pile.
last_rejected.fix: dragging along from their profitless occupations a great cloud of dust of cares
last_rejected.ruling: διατριβῶν = pastimes/occupations; φορυτόν = heap/refuse. Both renderings fall within normal range; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: the gates of hell were trampled down
last_rejected.why: ᾅδου is 'Hades,' the realm of the dead, not 'hell' (theological anachronism with wrong connotations).
last_rejected.fix: the gates of Hades were trampled down
last_rejected.ruling: ᾅδου = Hades/hell; 'hell' is standard equivalent in Christian translation tradition. No misleading reference.
